findingDispositions.framing: The capture's first screen ends above the timeline, so "bars align with the ruler" cannot be seen in it. Not a defect: tick placement and bar geometry are asserted mechanically (rulerAligned), and the expectation now reads "IF the timeline is in view".
findingDispositions.hairline: A 1 ms task on a 390 px track is a 1 CSS px mark. By design: data geometry is never enlarged (browser/README.md); the lane label and its outcome carry the task.
findingDispositions.refused: FIXED: the refused-report page no longer shows the search box or timeline controls, which could only do nothing there. They start hidden and the viewer reveals them only after admitting the data; acceptance.mjs asserts none is visible on a refused report (seen FAIL first), and the six refused captures were re-reviewed in run-13.
findingDispositions.offset-wrap: DEFERRED, cosmetic: the refusal map can wrap between a key and its value on a phone.
findingDispositions.focus: FIXED in this change: the dialog close handler took focus back after the user had moved on (an async `close` event). Close and Escape now restore focus synchronously, to the control that opened the dialog, found again by panel, row and label after a re-render; the queued `close` event is only a fallback for a close that skipped `cancel`, and it does nothing once the dialog has re-opened. Every path acts only while focus is lost. acceptance.mjs asserts a late close never steals focus, a stale close never takes a new opener, and focus returns to the right one of several identical track buttons when the browser did not focus it on click.
findingDispositions.residual-scroll: Noted by both reviewers, not a finding: after focus returns to the call to action, the full-height portrait capture stays scrolled 18 px where the other light captures sit at 0. The Light / dark control is fully in view at 0, so Playwright's click does not explain it; the cause is not established. No glyph is clipped.

limitations: Browser emulation, not physical iPhone testing.
WebKit fixed portrait/landscape only: its active-rotation probe fails a layout-width check, so rotation is not accepted.
WebKit offline context emulation disabled; both engines ran with --network none and every non-file request aborted.
A visual review is a lead, not a gate verdict; the reproducible checks are in acceptance.mjs.
